## Read This First: What This Document Actually Is

**13 of the 15 stories in scope were already implemented before this plan was
written.** For those, this is a **test-evidence audit**, not a plan. Only
**TUN-006** is genuinely forward-looking.

`/qa-plan`'s own guidance says a test plan written after implementation is a
post-mortem. That is accurate here and is stated rather than disguised. The
document still earns its place for four reasons:

1. It discharges the Sprint 1 Definition of Done, which requires this file.
2. It records, per story, which evidence exists and which is owed — the owed
   items are the sprint's actual remaining critical path.
3. It corrects a defect in the documented test command (see below).
4. It captures two `hazards.md` acceptance criteria that are assigned to
   `LevelValidation` but implemented by no rule.

For Sprint 2, run `/qa-plan sprint` **before** implementation begins.

## Finding 1 (BLOCKING for accuracy): The Documented Test Command Under-Runs the Suite

`tests/README.md` and the project's runner notes both document:

```bash
… --ignoreHeadlessMode -a res://tests/unit
```

That path excludes `tests/integration/`, which holds
`tests/integration/main/kill_area_death_test.gd` — **8 cases, and the automated
regression guard for BUG-0001**, the sprint's one open bug and the evidence for
CLR-002. Every "149/149 green" reported during this sprint silently omitted it.

Verified 2026-08-24: with both paths the suite is **157/157, 0 errors,
0 failures, 0 flaky, 0 skipped, 0 orphans, exit 0**. Nothing was broken — but
the guard for the open bug was not being exercised by the command in use.

**Use this command for every QA-relevant run from now on:**

```bash
"/c/00_repos/00-Godot-installer/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_win64.exe/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_win64_console.exe" \
  --headless --path . -s addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd \
  --ignoreHeadlessMode -c \
  -a res://tests/unit \
  -a res://tests/integration
```

Two flags carry weight:

- **`-a res://tests/integration`** — without it, 8 cases never run.
- **`-c`** — continue past the first failure (`tests/README.md:52`). Without it
  the runner stops at the first failing test, so a red run reports one failure
  and hides every later one. Observed across five deliberate-failure runs on
  2026-08-23. Do not read "1 failure" as "one thing is broken".

CI does **not** use this command — it calls `MikeSchulze/gdUnit4-action@v1`,
which is already given both paths. The under-reporting-on-red problem still
needs its own fix there, and belongs to CLR-005.

## Finding 2: Two `hazards.md` Criteria Are Assigned to `LevelValidation` With No Rule

`design/gdd/hazards.md` §8 states:

- **AC8** — "A level containing a hazard whose mask excludes the player layer
  fails `LevelValidation` at load"
- **AC9** — "A level whose spawn point overlaps a hazard fails `LevelValidation`
  at load"

Neither corresponds to any rule in ADR-0003 D3.3's seven-rule set
(`V-BUCKET-SUM`, `V-PLANT-MIN`, `V-OXY-CAP`, `V-GRAV-EXPORT`, `V-PROP-BUDGET`,
`V-WIRING`, `V-BOUNDS`). The GDD assigns work to a system that does not do it.

**This is recorded as an input to ARCH-1**, whose job is to sweep `hazards.md`
into `tr-registry.yaml`. It is deliberately **not** turned into invented test
cases here: whether these become new `V-` rules, move to a hazards epic, or are
withdrawn is an architecture decision, not a QA one. Flagging beats guessing.

## Automated Tests Required

### TUN-006 — CI greps for V6, V7 and V8 — Logic — NOT STARTED

The only story in this sprint needing tests written.

**Artifact**: a CI step in `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, following the shape of
the existing ADR-0004 D4.6 step.

**What to verify** — for each of V6, V7 and V8, the step must fail on a planted
violation and pass on the clean tree:

- The grep matches a real violation when one is planted.
- The grep does **not** match the legitimate declaration sites (the same
  carve-out the D4.6 step makes for `src/scripts/collision_layers.gd`).
- The step's exit code is decided explicitly. `grep` exits 1 when it finds
  nothing, which is the inverse of what a ban check needs. **A bare `grep` in a
  CI step passes forever.** The existing D4.6 step captures the match and
  branches on emptiness for exactly this reason — copy that structure.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Zero matches (clean tree) → step passes.
- A match inside a comment → the D4.6 step treats this as a deliberate, cheap
  false positive rather than solving comment-stripping. Follow that precedent
  and say so in the step's comment.
- A match in a `.tscn` rather than a `.gd` → scene files assign authored data
  legitimately. Scope `--include='*.gd'`, as D4.6 does.

**Estimated**: 3 CI assertions, verified by planting and reverting one violation
per ban. No gdUnit4 cases — this is a workflow step, not a runtime test.

### TUN-005 — one negative check never went red

`tuning_resources_test.gd` V1 is the GH#73615 type-identity guard. **It has never
been observed red.** Re-pointing a `.tres` at the wrong script is a **parse error
at load**, so the wrong-script route fails statically before any test runs and
cannot exercise V1.

**Do not "fix" this by weakening V1 to a null check.** The guard is correct; the
vector that would demonstrate it is unreachable by that route. Record it as a
known, accepted limitation. If a reachable vector is ever found, add it then.

> **Why the slider check is worth doing even though T4 settled the question.**
> T4 is VERIFIED TRUE: `@export_range` does **not** clamp and does **not** reject

> validator. The drag check confirms the *hint* is authored correctly — it does
> not and cannot confirm any enforcement. Where a knob must be clamped, clamp it
> in code. Evidence: `production/qa/evidence/t4-export-range-clamp-spike.md`.

## Smoke Test Scope

`tests/smoke/critical-paths.md` already holds 17 checks. **Sprint 1 added no
player-facing behaviour** — it delivered a constant registry, three resource
files, an accessor and a validation module, none of which is observable in
game. The list is therefore left as it is rather than padded.

Two existing entries carry this sprint's only in-game risk:

| # | Existing check | Sprint 1 relevance |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Touching a spike hazard kills the player, at any gravity orientation | Shares the death path CLR-002 repairs |
| 13 | Player death restarts the level and resets watering/bucket state | The out-of-bounds fall must produce this |

Run `/smoke-check sprint` once CLR-002's playtest passes — not before. A smoke
check that runs while the sprint's one open S2 bug is unverified reports a
build state that does not exist.

**Regression risk from Sprint 1 is low but not zero:** CLR-003 deleted nodes
from `player.tscn` and a mask line from `moving_platform.tscn`. Checks 4, 5 and
11 cover exactly that surface and should be run attentively.

## Playtest Requirements

| Story | Playtest goal | Min sessions | Target player |
|-------|--------------|--------------|---------------|
| CLR-002 | Does falling out of bounds in levels 05 and 06 restart the level, and does it read the same as any other death? | 1 | Anyone — this is a functional check, not a feel check |

**Sign-off**: notes written to
`production/session-logs/playtest-sprint-1-clr-002.md` and reviewed by qa-lead
before CLR-002 is marked Complete.

**Agent playtests do not settle this.** Agent-driven sessions misjudge pacing
and timing-dependent outcomes; a fall-and-restart is exactly that shape. One
human session is required.

No other story in this sprint needs a playtest — the remaining 14 are registry,
resource and validation work with no feel component.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when all of the following hold:

- [ ] Every acceptance criterion is verified — by a passing automated test, or
      by documented manual evidence with sign-off
- [ ] A test file exists at the specified path for every Logic and Integration
      story
- [ ] A manual evidence document exists for every story with an owed manual check
- [ ] The full suite passes with **both** paths and `-c` (157/157 as of
      2026-08-24) — not the unit path alone
- [ ] `/smoke-check sprint` passes, run **after** CLR-002's playtest
- [ ] No regressions introduced
- [ ] Code reviewed — done for this sprint's whole owed surface on 2026-08-24,
      verdict APPROVED WITH SUGGESTIONS, no blocking findings
- [ ] Story file set to `Status: Complete` via `/story-done`
- [ ] **BUG-0001 closed** — it is S2, and the sprint DoD forbids shipping an
      open S2 in a delivered feature
